title: POWER LADDER
why: You took a real rest day yesterday (swim + walk, 8h sleep) and came back fresh, so today cashes that recovery in on the one quality we've skipped all week: raw power. Everything so far has been density and conditioning — no explosive, low-rep work. So today is a double-bell power complex (clean → press → front squat, laddered — a format you've never run), a snappy snatch EMOM for ballistic power, and a tempo run for run variety (you've done intervals and easy steady, not tempo). Legs and arms are only lightly sore, so we load both but keep the reps crisp and the rest full — this is power, not a redline grind.

blocks.title: WARM-UP
blocks.text: 3 min easy jog @ 5.5 mph to raise core temp · Leg swings 10/side · World's-greatest-stretch 4/side · Halos 5 each way (16 kg) · Prying goblet squat ×5 (16 kg) · 10 light two-hand swings (16 kg) to fire the hips before the complex.

blocks.title: POWER COMPLEX
blocks.meta: ~18 min · double 40s · clean → press → front squat
blocks.text: The complex: 1 clean + 1 press + 1 front squat, then 2 of each, then 3 of each — all unbroken, bells never set down (that's 6 cleans, 6 presses, 6 front squats per round). Rest a FULL 90s, repeat for 4 rounds. This is a power/strength piece, not a burner: drive every clean and press explosively, own the squats, stop each ladder with a rep or two in the tank. If the presses stall, drop to a single 40 for the press portion. New format for you — flow it like one movement.

blocks.title: SNATCH POWER
blocks.workRest: 10 reps on the top of each minute, rest the remainder
blocks.text: Every minute on the minute for 10 minutes: 5 snatches per side (10 total), then rest whatever's left in the minute — should be 25-40s. This is pure ballistic power: snap the hips, punch through the top, float it back down. Keep the reps fast and crisp; if they start slowing, cut to 8/min. Set the EMOM/COUNTDOWN timer to 10 rounds of 1:00.

blocks.title: TEMPO RUN
blocks.text: Steady comfortably-hard tempo — the run gear you haven't touched this week (intervals and easy steady, yes; tempo, no). Hold 7.0 mph the whole way: breathing hard but controlled, not gasping. If the complex left your legs heavy, this is a green light to drop to 6.3 mph and just hold Zone 2 — don't turn it into a grind. Tall posture, quick feet, relaxed shoulders.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.text: Walk 2 min @ 3 mph · Stretch 30s each: shoulders/lats, thoracic opener, quads, hip flexors, hamstrings · 5 slow deep breaths to finish.
